content: (a) Findings.--The General Assembly hereby finds that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.1. Designation of “Lithuanian Independence Day”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.1. Designation of “Lithuanian Independence Day”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.1. Designation of “Lithuanian Independence Day” (2023)
content:
In order to publicly recognize the outstanding contributions made by the Lithuanian
   people to the heritage of America and this Commonwealth, February 16 of each year
   is designated as “Lithuanian Independence Day.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.2. Designation of Rachel Carson Day
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.2. Designation of Rachel Carson Day
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.2. Designation of Rachel Carson Day (2023)
content:
In recognition of Rachel Carson, who was born on May 27, 1907, and who is generally
   recognized as the “Mother of the Age of Ecology,” May 27 of each year is hereby designated
   “Rachel Carson Day” and is set aside to commemorate the birth of Rachel Carson.  The Governor is authorized and directed to issue a proclamation each year calling
   upon the people of this Commonwealth to commemorate the life and contributions of
   Rachel Carson and to observe that day with appropriate honors and ceremonies.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.13. Designation of “Diwali Day”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.13. Designation of “Diwali Day”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.13. Designation of “Diwali Day” (2023)
content:
In accordance with the official day recognized by the Indian government, the 15th
   day of the Hindu lunisolar month of Kartik shall be designated “Diwali Day” in this
   Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.3. Designation of “Pennsylvania POW/MIA Recognition Day”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.3. Designation of “Pennsylvania POW/MIA Recognition Day”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.3. Designation of “Pennsylvania POW/MIA Recognition Day” (2023)
content:
In recognition of the fact that the number of American POW/MIA's still missing and
   unaccounted for in Southeast Asia is 2,282 (116 Pennsylvanians), in the Korean War,
   8,100, in World War II, 78,000, and in the Persian Gulf War, 9, and whose bravery,
   patriotism and courage will never be forgotten by their loved ones and their grateful
   Nation and Commonwealth, the third Friday of September of each year is hereby designated
   “Pennsylvania POW/MIA Recognition Day.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.7. Designation of “Earth Day”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.7. Designation of “Earth Day”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.7. Designation of “Earth Day” (2023)
content:
In recognition of “Earth Day,” which was first celebrated on April 22, 1970, and has
   since been celebrated annually by people from around the world to demonstrate a collective
   concern for the environment, April 22 of each year is hereby designated “Earth Day”
   in Pennsylvania.  The Governor is authorized and directed to issue a proclamation each year calling
   upon the citizens of this Commonwealth to participate in events and activities to
   help protect and improve the environmental quality of Pennsylvania and the planet.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.8. Designation of “Commonwealth Day of Prayer and Celebration of Religious Freedom”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.8. Designation of “Commonwealth Day of Prayer and Celebration of Religious Freedom”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.8. Designation of “Commonwealth Day of Prayer and Celebration of Religious Freedom” (2023)
content:
The first Thursday in May of each year shall be designated “Commonwealth Day of Prayer
   and Celebration of Religious Freedom,” on which the people of this Commonwealth may
   turn to God in prayer and meditation and on which freedom of religion in this Commonwealth
   may be celebrated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.5. Firefighters' memorial
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.5. Firefighters' memorial
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.5. Firefighters' memorial (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The Sunday which marks the beginning of Fire Prevention Week of every year is designated
      as “Firefighters' Memorial Sunday” to honor paid and volunteer firefighters who have
      died during the previous year, either in the line of duty or of natural causes or
      off-duty accidents.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 19.2. Last Friday in April
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 19.2. Last Friday in April
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 19.2. Last Friday in April (2023)
content: The day designated as Arbor Day shall be the last Friday in April.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.9. Designation of “Rosa Parks Remembrance Day”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.9. Designation of “Rosa Parks Remembrance Day”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.9. Designation of “Rosa Parks Remembrance Day” (2023)
content:
Annually the first Monday following February 4th, the birthday of Rosa Parks, is designated
   as Rosa Parks Remembrance Day, a day to remember the courage of the “Mother of the
   Civil Rights Movement” and her contribution to the history and culture of this nation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.10. Agriculture Day and Week designation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.10. Agriculture Day and Week designation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.10. Agriculture Day and Week designation (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--Except as set forth in subsection (b), the following apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.12. Designation of “Juneteenth National Freedom Day”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.12. Designation of “Juneteenth National Freedom Day”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.12. Designation of “Juneteenth National Freedom Day” (2023)
content: June 19 is designated as “Juneteenth National Freedom Day” in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›General Provisions›PA ST 44 P.S. § 48. Display of United States and POW/MIA flags; regulation by Governor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › General Provisions › PA ST 44 P.S. § 48. Display of United States and POW/MIA flags; regulation by Governor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 48. Display of United States and POW/MIA flags; regulation by Governor (2023)
content:
(a) The Governor of the Commonwealth shall have the sole power and duty for regulating
      the display of the flag of the United States from any public ground or building of
      the Commonwealth, of any board, commission or authority of the Commonwealth created
      by the General Assembly, of any political subdivision of the Commonwealth, of any
      school district of the Commonwealth, or from any ground or building of any institution
      which receives any State aid from the Commonwealth.  The Governor shall have the power and duty to promulgate rules and regulations pursuant
      to the provisions of this section and such rules and regulations shall be in compliance
      with the National Flag Code.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›General Provisions›PA ST 44 P.S. § 42. Flags other than Stars and Stripes on public buildings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › General Provisions › PA ST 44 P.S. § 42. Flags other than Stars and Stripes on public buildings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 42. Flags other than Stars and Stripes on public buildings (2023)
content:
No other flag than the Stars and Stripes, which is our national emblem, shall be allowed
   to wave from any public building in this Commonwealth, except such as may be occupied
   by a duly accredited minister or consul of a foreign civil power to these United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.11. Bill of Rights Day
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.11. Bill of Rights Day
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 40.11. Bill of Rights Day (2023)
content:
In recognition of the Bill of Rights, the first ten amendments to the Constitution
   of the United States of America, which was ratified on December 15, 1791, December
   15 of each year is hereby designated as “Bill of Rights Day.”  The Governor is authorized and requested to issue a proclamation each year recognizing
   the significance of the Bill of Rights in our lives and calling upon the people of
   this Commonwealth to commemorate the day with appropriate ceremonies and educational
   activities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›General Provisions›PA ST 44 P.S. § 44. Display of county and municipal flags
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › General Provisions › PA ST 44 P.S. § 44. Display of county and municipal flags
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 44. Display of county and municipal flags (2023)
content:
After the approval of this act it shall be lawful to display the flag of any county,
   city, borough, or other municipality in the State on the public buildings of any county,
   city, borough, or other municipality of the State.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›General Provisions›PA ST 44 P.S. § 41. National flag to be raised over capitol at all times
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › General Provisions › PA ST 44 P.S. § 41. National flag to be raised over capitol at all times
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 41. National flag to be raised over capitol at all times (2023)
content:
The national flag [shall] be raised over the capitol buildings at all times, and that
   the superintendent of public grounds and buildings be required to carry this resolution
   into effect.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›General Provisions›PA ST 44 P.S. § 45. Flag of Pennsylvania; size and emblems
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › General Provisions › PA ST 44 P.S. § 45. Flag of Pennsylvania; size and emblems
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 45. Flag of Pennsylvania; size and emblems (2023)
content:
The flag to be known as the official flag of the commonwealth of Pennsylvania shall
   be of blue, same color as the blue field in the flag of the United States, and of
   the following dimensions and design;  to wit, The length, or height of the staff to
   be nine feet, including brass spearhead and ferrule;  the fly of the said flag to
   be six feet two inches, and to be four feet six inches on the staff;  in the center
   of the flag there shall be embroidered in silk the same on both sides of the flag
   the coat of arms of the commonwealth of Pennsylvania, in proportionate size;  the
   edges to be trimmed with knotted fringe of yellow silk, two and one-half inches wide;
   a cord, with tassels, to be attached to the staff, at the spearhead, to be eight feet
   six inches long, and composed of white and blue silk strands.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›General Provisions›PA ST 44 P.S. § 44.1. Display of state flag at certain memorials and funerals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › General Provisions › PA ST 44 P.S. § 44.1. Display of state flag at certain memorials and funerals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 44.1. Display of state flag at certain memorials and funerals (2023)
content:
It shall be lawful to display the flag of Pennsylvania over a memorial, a casket and
   at a funeral procession of a deceased individual who was a member or employe of a
   volunteer or municipal police department, fire department, ambulance service or rescue
   squad or a fire police organization.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›General Provisions›PA ST 44 P.S. § 43. State flag may be displayed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › General Provisions › PA ST 44 P.S. § 43. State flag may be displayed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 43. State flag may be displayed (2023)
content:
After the approval of this act it shall be lawful to display the flag of Pennsylvania
   on any public building in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances›PA ST 44 P.S. § 32. Columbus Day
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 2. Other Holidays and Observances › PA ST 44 P.S. § 32. Columbus Day
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 32. Columbus Day (2023)
content:
The Governor shall issue, annually, his Proclamation designating and setting apart
   October 12 as Columbus Day, and calling upon the people of the Commonwealth, the public
   schools and other educational institutions and historical organizations to observe
   the discovery of the New World with appropriate exercises and programs, to the end
   that the discovery of America shall be commemorated each year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›General Provisions›PA ST 44 P.S. § 47. Secretary of commonwealth to provide model flag
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › General Provisions › PA ST 44 P.S. § 47. Secretary of commonwealth to provide model flag
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 47. Secretary of commonwealth to provide model flag (2023)
content:
The secretary of the commonwealth is hereby directed to provide a flag, in accordance
   with the description given in the first section of this act,1and keep the same deposited in the office of the secretary of the commonwealth, as
   a model;  the cost of said flag to be paid by warrant of the auditor general upon
   the state treasurer;  and for this purpose the sum of one hundred and fifty dollars,
   or so much thereof as may be necessary, is hereby specifically appropriated, out of
   any moneys in the state treasury not otherwise appropriated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›General Provisions›PA ST 44 P.S. § 48.1. Proper display of flags
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › General Provisions › PA ST 44 P.S. § 48.1. Proper display of flags
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 48.1. Proper display of flags (2023)
content:
A person is authorized to display any flag of the United States or the Commonwealth
   inside or outside of that person's residence in any manner, provided that the display
   is not in violation of18 Pa.C.S. § 2102(relating to desecration of flag) and is not in violation of the zoning or regulatory
   authority of the Commonwealth or any political subdivision.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›American, Commonwealth and Military Flag Act›PA ST 44 P.S. § 50.3. Display of American flag, Commonwealth flag and military flag
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › American, Commonwealth and Military Flag Act › PA ST 44 P.S. § 50.3. Display of American flag, Commonwealth flag and military flag
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 50.3. Display of American flag, Commonwealth flag and military flag (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Notwithstanding any provision in the association's declaration, covenants, bylaws,
      rules, regulations or other instruments or any construction of any of those instruments
      by an association's executive board, an association may not prohibit the outdoor display
      of one American flag, Commonwealth flag and military flag by a unit owner on that
      unit owner's property or property within the exclusive control of a unit owner or
      that portion of an exterior wall directly attached to the unit if the American flag
      is displayed in a manner consistent with4 U.S.C. § 4(relating to pledge of allegiance to the flag;  manner of delivery) through 10 (relating
      to modification of rules and customs by President) and a Commonwealth flag or military
      flag is displayed in accordance with any rules and regulations adopted by the association.  An association may adopt rules and regulations, consistent with4 U.S.C. § 4through10, regarding the placement and manner of display of the American flag, and an association
      may adopt rules and regulations regarding the placement and manner of display of a
      Commonwealth flag or military flag.  An association may adopt rules and regulations regarding the location, size and
      use of a flagpole but cannot prohibit the use of wall brackets to display the American
      flag, Commonwealth flag and military flag.  The size of the American flag, Commonwealth flag and military flag to be flown shall
      not be larger than five feet by three feet.  In addition, any rules and regulations adopted by the association regarding the
      display of a military flag must permit the flying of such flags, in a respectful way,
      on President's Day, Iwo Jima Flag Raising Day, Vietnam Veterans Day, V-E Day, Armed
      Forces Day, Memorial Day, Flag Day, Independence Day, Korean War Veterans Armistice
      Day, V-J Day, Patriot's Day, POW/MIA Recognition Day, Veterans Day, Pearl Harbor Day
      and the birthday of each branch of the United States Armed Forces.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›American, Commonwealth and Military Flag Act›PA ST 44 P.S. § 50.2. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › American, Commonwealth and Military Flag Act › PA ST 44 P.S. § 50.2. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 50.2. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this act shall have the meanings given
   to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›Honor and Remember Flag Act›PA ST 44 P.S. § 51. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › Honor and Remember Flag Act › PA ST 44 P.S. § 51. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 51. Short title (2023)
content: This act shall be known and may be cited as the Honor and Remember Flag Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›American, Commonwealth and Military Flag Act›PA ST 44 P.S. § 50.1. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › American, Commonwealth and Military Flag Act › PA ST 44 P.S. § 50.1. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 50.1. Short title (2023)
content:
This act shall be known and may be cited as the American, Commonwealth and Military
   Flag Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›Honor and Remember Flag Act›PA ST 44 P.S. § 52. Official adoption of flag
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › Honor and Remember Flag Act › PA ST 44 P.S. § 52. Official adoption of flag
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 52. Official adoption of flag (2023)
content:
The Honor and Remember Flag created by Honor and Remember, Inc., is hereby adopted
   as this Commonwealth's emblem of the service and sacrifice of the brave men and women
   of the United States Armed Forces who have given their lives in the line of duty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›Emergency Medical Services Memorial Flag›PA ST 44 P.S. § 61. Emergency medical services memorial flag
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › Emergency Medical Services Memorial Flag › PA ST 44 P.S. § 61. Emergency medical services memorial flag
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 61. Emergency medical services memorial flag (2023)
content: (a) Establishment.--An emergency medical services memorial flag is established for this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›Emergency Medical Services Memorial Flag›PA ST 44 P.S. § 62. Use of flag
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › Emergency Medical Services Memorial Flag › PA ST 44 P.S. § 62. Use of flag
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 62. Use of flag (2023)
content:
The emergency medical services memorial flag may be displayed over emergency medical
   service memorials and emergency medical service funeral processions and from the poles
   of any public ground or political subdivision for a period of not more than seven
   days after the death of a member of any emergency medical service, and as further
   directed by the Director of Emergency Medical Services in the Department of Health.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›Emergency Medical Services Memorial Flag›PA ST 44 P.S. § 64. Limitation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › Emergency Medical Services Memorial Flag › PA ST 44 P.S. § 64. Limitation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 64. Limitation (2023)
content:
Authorized utilization of the emergency medical services memorial flag by the Commonwealth
   or an entity of the Commonwealth shall not constitute a presumption of eligibility
   or be admissible as evidence for a claim under the act of June 24, 1976 (P.L. 424,
   No. 101),1referred to as the Emergency and Law Enforcement Personnel Death Benefits Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›Honor and Remember Flag Act›PA ST 44 P.S. § 53. Duty of Department of General Services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › Honor and Remember Flag Act › PA ST 44 P.S. § 53. Duty of Department of General Services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 53. Duty of Department of General Services (2023)
content:
The Department of General Services shall forthwith arrange for and permanently place
   the Honor and Remember Flag in Soldiers' Grove.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances›Chapter 3. Flags›Emergency Medical Services Memorial Flag›PA ST 44 P.S. § 63. Agency responsibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 44 P.S. Legal Holidays and Observances › Chapter 3. Flags › Emergency Medical Services Memorial Flag › PA ST 44 P.S. § 63. Agency responsibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 44 P.S. § 63. Agency responsibility (2023)
content:
The Bureau of Emergency Medical Services in the Department of Health shall maintain
   the official flag and have the responsibility to implement the provisions of this
   act and oversee the production, acquisition and distribution of the flag.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1208. Unfiled regulations invalid
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1208. Unfiled regulations invalid
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1208. Unfiled regulations invalid (2023)
content:
An administrative regulation or change therein promulgated after the effective date
   of this act shall not be valid for any purpose until filed by1the Legislative Reference Bureau, as provided in section 409.2

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 1. Advertisements›Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 45 P.S. § 33. Copy of advertisement to be accompanied with order for publication
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 1. Advertisements › Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 45 P.S. § 33. Copy of advertisement to be accompanied with order for publication
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 33. Copy of advertisement to be accompanied with order for publication (2023)
content:
All officers who may be authorized to advertise as aforesaid, shall accompany each
   copy of the advertisements, furnished by them for publication, with an order, stating
   the number of lines or squares such advertisements are each to occupy when inserted,
   and the number of insertions which is to be given to each of the same.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1202. Adoption of regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1202. Adoption of regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1202. Adoption of regulations (2023)
content:
Before taking action upon any administrative regulation or change therein the agency
   shall review and consider any written comments submitted pursuant to section 2011and may hold such public hearings as seem appropriate.  If the act of Assembly or other authority under which a regulation is proposed to
   be promulgated, amended or repealed requires the holding of public hearings or establishes
   other procedures in addition to those prescribed by this Article II,2the agency shall hold public hearings or comply with such other procedures as are
   not inconsistent with the provisions of this act.  The agency text of any administrative regulation or change therein as finally adopted
   may contain such modifications to the proposed text as published pursuant to section
   201 as do not enlarge its original purpose, but modifications which enlarge the original
   purpose of a proposal as published under section 201 shall be republished thereunder
   prior to final adoption by the agency.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article I. Short Title and Definitions›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1102. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article I. Short Title and Definitions › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1102. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1102. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and terms shall have the following meanings, unless the context
   clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1206. Format of regulations and other documents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1206. Format of regulations and other documents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1206. Format of regulations and other documents (2023)
content:
The agency text of all regulations and other documents, required or authorized to
   be deposited with the Legislative Reference Bureau by this act shall be prepared in
   such form and format as may be prescribed by regulations promulgated by the joint
   committee.  Such regulations shall require that every administrative regulation or change therein
   indicate expressly the statutory or other authority under which it is promulgated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1204. Omission of notice of proposed rule making
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1204. Omission of notice of proposed rule making
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1204. Omission of notice of proposed rule making (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided by regulations promulgated by the joint committee, an
   agency may omit or modify the procedures specified in sections 201 and 202,1if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 1. Advertisements›Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 45 P.S. § 34. Bill to be accompanied by order and affidavit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 1. Advertisements › Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 45 P.S. § 34. Bill to be accompanied by order and affidavit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 34. Bill to be accompanied by order and affidavit (2023)
content:
It shall not be lawful for the auditor general to issue warrants to pay for any advertisement
   authorized by law, unless the bills for the same be accompanied with the written or
   printed, or partly written and printed order of the officer or officers furnishing
   the same for publication, stating the number of lines or squares it is to occupy when
   inserted, and the number of insertions to be given to it, together with the affidavit
   of the editor or publisher of the paper publishing the same, that it has been inserted
   in all respects as ordered.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article VI. General Provisions›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1602. Appropriation; distribution of publication expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article VI. General Provisions › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1602. Appropriation; distribution of publication expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1602. Appropriation; distribution of publication expenses (2023)
content:
The sum of one hundred seventy-five thousand dollars ($175,000) is hereby appropriated
   for the purposes of this act of which twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) is appropriated
   to the Legislative Reference Bureau and one hundred fifty thousand dollars ($150,000)
   is appropriated to the Department of Property and Supplies.1In order to reimburse the Legislative Reference Bureau for the cost of administering
   this act and in order to reimburse the Department of Property and Supplies for the
   expenses of the joint committee and for the costs incurred in printing and distributing
   the publications provided for in Article IV2which are neither recovered by the sale of such publications to an agency under sections
   410 and 4123or to the public under section 6014nor paid by subsequent appropriations made directly to the bureau or the department
   for the costs and expenses of such administration, printing and distribution, every
   agency or court issuing, prescribing or promulgating documents published by authority
   of this act shall be billed at least quarterly by the bureau and the Department of
   Property and Supplies, upon a cost basis, at such amounts as the joint committee with
   the approval of the Executive Board shall determine for such costs and expenses, including
   costs incurred pursuant to section 403.5Amounts payable hereunder for reimbursing the bureau and the department for the
   costs of administration and printing and distribution shall be credited to the appropriations
   of the bureau and the department respectively, and shall be paid out of the moneys
   in the General Fund, special operating funds, or other funds of the State Treasury
   currently appropriated to each such issuing, prescribing or promulgating agency or
   court.  Nothing in this section shall limit the right of the General Assembly to make annual
   appropriations to the bureau or to the department or both for their total anticipated
   costs and expenses under this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1203. Effective date of regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1203. Effective date of regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1203. Effective date of regulations (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided by regulations promulgated by the joint committee, the
   effective date specified in any administrative regulation or change therein subject
   to the provisions of sections 201 and 2021shall be not less than thirty days after the notice of proposed rule making required
   thereby has been given unless:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1205. Approval as to legality
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1205. Approval as to legality
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1205. Approval as to legality (2023)
content:
All administrative regulations and changes therein shall be approved as to legality
   by the Department of Justice before they are deposited with the Legislative Reference
   Bureau pursuant to section 207.1In the event the Department of Justice shall rule illegal all or any part of any
   administrative regulations or changes therein, adopted by an agency which is by law
   independent of the policy supervision and control of the Governor, and such agency
   or party before such agency supporting such regulations or changes therein shall disagree
   with the ruling of the Department of Justice, such agency or such party may appeal
   from the determination of the department to the Commonwealth Court, whereupon the
   court shall direct the department to approve those parts of the administrative regulations
   or changes therein ruled illegal which the court finds to be legal.  In all other cases the decision of the Department of Justice shall be final and
   shall not be subject to any form of judicial review at the instance of the agency,
   or any supporting party, but nothing in this section shall affect the right of any
   person adversely affected by a regulation or change therein to obtain a determination
   of the validity thereof in any appropriate proceeding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 1. Advertisements›Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 45 P.S. § 31. Publication of advertisements by officers; rates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 1. Advertisements › Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 45 P.S. § 31. Publication of advertisements by officers; rates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 31. Publication of advertisements by officers; rates (2023)
content:
All advertisements, published by any officer or officers of this commonwealth authorized
   by law to publish the same, shall be published only in the regular advertising columns
   of the papers to which they are furnished, without being leaded or displayed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1201. Notice of proposed rule making
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1201. Notice of proposed rule making
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1201. Notice of proposed rule making (2023)
content:
Except as provided in section 2041an agency shall give, in the manner provided in section 4052(relating to additional contents of temporary supplements) public notice of its intention
   to promulgate, amend or repeal any administrative regulation.  Such notice shall include:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices›Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law›Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents›PA ST 45 P.S. § 1207. Deposit of agency text of regulations required
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 P.S. Legal Notices › Chapter 5. Commonwealth Documents Law › Article II. Promulgation of Regulations and Format of Documents › PA ST 45 P.S. § 1207. Deposit of agency text of regulations required
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 P.S. § 1207. Deposit of agency text of regulations required (2023)
content:
The agency text of all administrative and other regulations, and changes therein,
   certified by the executive officer, chairman or secretary of the agency, shall be
   deposited with the Legislative Reference Bureau in the manner required by section
   409.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 1. General Provisions›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 1. General Provisions › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Definitions (2023)
content:
(a) Definitions applicable to printing or newspaper advertising laws.--Subject to additional definitions contained in subsequent provisions of this title
      which are applicable to specific provisions of this title, the following words and
      phrases when used in:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 306. Use of trade publications
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 306. Use of trade publications
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 306. Use of trade publications (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any government unit which is required by law to advertise for bids for public works,
      contracts, supplies or equipment, may, in its discretion, authorize the publication
      of such advertising, in addition to the newspapers authorized by the other provisions
      of this chapter, also in any publication or journal devoted to the dissemination of
      information about construction work published in this Commonwealth at least once a
      week and circulating among contractors, manufacturers and dealers doing business in
      the community in which such public works are to be constructed or supplies or equipment
      purchased.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Charges taxable as costs and administration expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Charges taxable as costs and administration expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Charges taxable as costs and administration expenses (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided by general rule, all charges, costs, and expenses incurred,
   including the fees for affidavits to proofs of publication, for official and legal
   advertising in any matter by any person shall be taxable, collectible and payable
   as other court costs and expenses of administration are required by law to be taxed,
   collected, and paid, upon all decrees of court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Level of advertising rates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Level of advertising rates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Level of advertising rates (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All official and legal advertising shall be charged for at an established or declared
      rate or price per single column, line of reading matter measured in depth by the point
      system, or at a rate or price per inch single column.  When such official and legal advertising is not classified and is not published
      according to prescribed or recognized forms, and no rate has been established or declared,
      such rate for official and legal advertising shall not be in excess of the rates usually
      charged or received by the publication publishing such official and legal advertising
      for commercial, general, or other advertising.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 308. Additional publication in legal journals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 308. Additional publication in legal journals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 308. Additional publication in legal journals (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided by statute, every notice or advertisement required
      by law or rule of court to be published in one or more newspapers of general circulation,
      unless dispensed with by special order of court, shall also be published in the legal
      newspaper, issued at least weekly, in the county, designated by rules of court for
      the publication of court or other legal notices, if such newspaper exists.  Publication in such legal newspaper shall be made as often as required to be made
      in such newspapers in general circulation, and shall be subject to the same stipulations
      and regulations as those imposed for the like services upon all newspapers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 302. Scope and interpretation of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 302. Scope and interpretation of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 302. Scope and interpretation of chapter (2023)
content: The provisions of this chapter are intended to be a comprehensive statute:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 309. Inclusion of common geographical names
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 309. Inclusion of common geographical names
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 309. Inclusion of common geographical names (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Whenever official advertising or legal advertising involves a road, street, highway,
      bridge, municipality, village or boundary, the advertisement shall, in order that
      it may readily be understood by inhabitants of the area involved, include the common,
      local or general usage designation of every such road, street, highway, bridge, municipality,
      village or boundary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Short title of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Short title of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Short title of chapter (2023)
content: This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Newspaper Advertising Act.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 307. Effect of failure to advertise when required
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 307. Effect of failure to advertise when required
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 307. Effect of failure to advertise when required (2023)
content:
No legal proceeding, matter, or case in which notice is required to be given by official
   or legal advertising, shall be binding and effective upon any interested person unless
   such official and legal advertising is printed and published in the newspapers of
   general circulation, official newspapers, and legal newspapers defined by this title,
   in the manner and as required by statute, and by any rule, order, or decree of court,
   resolution of a corporation, or unincorporated association, or ordinance, rule, or
   regulation of any government unit, in the proper newspapers of general circulation,
   official newspapers, and legal newspapers, defined by this title, and a proof of publication
   is filed of record in such matter or proceeding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 5. General Provisions›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Judicial notice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 5. General Provisions › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Judicial notice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Judicial notice (2023)
content:
The contents of the code, of the permanent supplements thereto, and of the bulletin,
   shall be judicially noticed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 5. General Provisions›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. General administration of part
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 5. General Provisions › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. General administration of part
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. General administration of part (2023)
content:
Subject to the provisions of section 732 (relating to required contractual arrangements),
   the manner in which the code, the permanent supplements thereto, and the bulletin,
   shall be published, and all other matters with respect thereto not otherwise provided
   for in this part shall be prescribed by regulations promulgated or orders adopted
   by the joint committee.  The joint committee shall administer this part and Subchapter A of Chapter 3 of
   Title 2 (relating to regulations of Commonwealth agencies) with a view toward encouraging
   the widest possible dissemination of documents among the persons affected thereby
   which is consistent with the due administration of public affairs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 310. No unauthorized advertisements to be published
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 310. No unauthorized advertisements to be published
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 310. No unauthorized advertisements to be published (2023)
content:
No advertisement shall be published by any court or other government unit, which is
   not duly authorized by law, nor in more papers than so authorized.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 5. General Provisions›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 5. General Provisions › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Definitions

content:

   which are applicable to specific provisions of this part, the following words and
   phrases when used in this part shall have, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise,
   the meanings given to them in this section:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 5. General Provisions›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 505. Distribution of publication expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 5. General Provisions › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 505. Distribution of publication expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 505. Distribution of publication expenses (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In order to reimburse the Legislative Reference Bureau for the cost of administering
      this part and in order to reimburse the Department of General Services for the expenses
      of the joint committee and for the costs incurred in publication under Subchapter
      B of Chapter 71(relating to publication of documents) which are neither recovered by the sale of
      such publications to an agency under section 729 (relating to publication of individual
      documents) nor paid by appropriations made directly to the bureau or the department
      for the costs and expenses of such publication, every government unit issuing, prescribing
      or promulgating documents published by authority of this part shall be billed at least
      quarterly by the bureau and the Department of General Services, upon a cost basis,
      at such amounts as the joint committee with the approval of the Executive Board shall
      determine, for such costs and expenses.  Amounts payable under this section for reimbursing the bureau and the department
      for the costs shall be credited to the appropriations of the bureau and the department
      respectively, and shall be paid out of the moneys in the General Fund, special operating
      funds, or other funds of the State Treasury currently appropriated to each such issuing,
      prescribing or promulgating government unit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Legal Advertising›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Establishment and change of advertising rates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Legal Advertising › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Establishment and change of advertising rates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Establishment and change of advertising rates (2023)
content:
All newspapers of general circulation, official newspapers and legal newspapers accepting
   and publishing official and legal advertising, are hereby required to fix and establish
   rates and charges for official, legal and all other kinds of advertising, offered
   or accepted for publication, and such publications shall furnish, on demand, to any
   person having use for the same, detailed schedules, stating the rates and charges
   which shall be deemed to be in force and effect until changed or altered, and, when
   changed or altered, such publication shall give the person authorized or required
   to publish advertising, before demanding or receiving compensation at any increased
   rate, notice that the rates and charges of such publication for advertising have been
   changed or abrogated, and that increased advertising rates and charges have been established
   or fixed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 5. General Provisions›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Joint Committee on Documents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 5. General Provisions › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Joint Committee on Documents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Joint Committee on Documents (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--The Joint Committee on Documents shall consist of nine governmental members and two
      public members.  The governmental members shall be the General Counsel, the Attorney General, the
      Director of the Legislative Reference Bureau, the Director of the Pennsylvania Code,
      the President pro tempore of the Senate, the Minority Leader of the Senate, the Speaker
      of the House of Representatives, the Minority Leader of the House of Representatives
      and the Secretary of General Services, or persons severally designated in writing
      by them.  The public members shall be appointed by the Governor from among attorneys at law
      or other members of the public who represent the class who may be expected to refer
      to the documents published pursuant to this part.  For the purposes of the act of April 9, 1929 (P.L. 177, No. 175), known as “The
      Administrative Code of 1929”1and its supplements the joint committee shall be a departmental administrative board
      in the Department of General Services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 5. General Provisions›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 507. Form of citation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 5. General Provisions › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 507. Form of citation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 507. Form of citation (2023)
content:
Without prejudice to any other mode of citation the code and permanent supplements
   thereto may be cited by title and section number, and the bulletin may be cited by
   volume and page number.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 5. General Provisions›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 508. Effect of future legislation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 5. General Provisions › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 508. Effect of future legislation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 508. Effect of future legislation (2023)
content:
No subsequent statute shall be held to supersede or modify the act of July 31, 1968
   (P.L. 769, No. 240),1referred to as the Commonwealth Documents Law, or this part except to the extent
   that such statute shall do so expressly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 5. General Provisions›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 509. Format of documents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 5. General Provisions › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 509. Format of documents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 509. Format of documents (2023)
content:
The agency text of all documents required to be deposited with the Legislative Reference
   Bureau by this part shall be in such form and format as may be prescribed by regulations
   promulgated by the joint committee.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Subchapter A. Codification of Regulations and Other Documents›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Official codification created
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Subchapter A. Codification of Regulations and Other Documents › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Official codification created
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Official codification created (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of the Legislative Reference Bureau, subject to the policy supervision
   and direction of the joint committee, to compile, edit and supplement or to contract
   through the department for the compilation, editing and supplementation of an official
   legal codification, to be divided into titles of convenient size and scope, and to
   be known as the “Pennsylvania Code.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 7. Codification and Publication of Documents›Subchapter B. Publication of Documents›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 721. Publication of official codification
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 7. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 721. Publication of official codification (2023)
content:

   subchapter and regulations promulgated hereunder.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 7. Codification and Publication of Documents›Subchapter B. Publication of Documents›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 723. Processing of deposited documents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 7. Codification and Publication of Documents › Subchapter B. Publication of Documents › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 723. Processing of deposited documents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 723. Processing of deposited documents (2023)
content:
(a) Review of deposited text.--The bureau, or a qualified contractor selected by the bureau with the approval of
      the joint committee, may review any or all documents deposited with the bureau before
      they are released for publication, and may prepare in active cooperation with an agency
      a revised text of any document relating to the administrative regulations of the agency
      which conforms fully to the format established for the code, which eliminates all
      obsolete, unnecessary or unauthorized material, which has been prepared in such a
      manner as to lend to the published code as a whole uniformity of style and clarity
      of expression, and which does not effect any change in the substance of the deposited
      text of such regulations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 7. Codification and Publication of Documents›Subchapter B. Publication of Documents›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 722. Deposit of documents required
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices › Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents › Chapter 7. Codification and Publication of Documents › Subchapter B. Publication of Documents › PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 722. Deposit of documents required
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 722. Deposit of documents required (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Two duplicate original copies, certified by the executive officer, chairman or secretary
      of the agency, or by the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts or the clerk
      or prothonotary of the Supreme Court, in the case of a judicial document, of any document
      required or authorized to be published under this subchapter, shall be deposited with
      the Legislative Reference Bureau.  If the bureau finds that such document has been approved as to legality, if such
      approval is required by2 Pa.C.S. § 305(relating to approval as to legality), and is in the form and format required by
      any applicable regulations promulgated under2 Pa.C.S. § 306(relating to format of regulations) or section 509 of this title (relating to format
      of documents), it shall file such document, assign thereto and indicate thereon a
      distinctive serial number, and indicate thereon the date and time of filing.

content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (c), all documents required or authorized by section
      702 (relating to contents of Pennsylvania Code) to be codified in the code, and all
      other documents required or authorized by section 725 (relating to additional contents

content:
(a) General rule.--The code and the permanent supplements thereto shall be published pursuant to typographical
      and contractual arrangements which shall ensure to every agency and the unified judicial
      system an opportunity to procure at reasonable cost individually printed pamphlet

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 7. Codification and Publication of Documents›Subchapter B. Publication of Documents›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 726. Permanent supplements to Pennsylvania Code

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 726. Permanent supplements to Pennsylvania Code (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--At least once each year all documents required or authorized pursuant to section 702
      (relating to contents of Pennsylvania Code) to be codified in the code which have
      been filed with the bureau pursuant to this part shall be permanently integrated into
      the code by publication pursuant to section 721 (relating to publication of official
      codification).  The index to the code shall be similarly supplemented.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 45 Pa.C.S.A. Legal Notices›Part II. Publication and Effectiveness of Commonwealth Documents›Chapter 7. Codification and Publication of Documents›Subchapter B. Publication of Documents›PA ST 45 Pa.C.S.A. § 728. Matter not permitted to be published

content:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this part no press release, speech, or other
   unofficial comments or news material shall be published in the code, the permanent
   supplements thereto, or in the bulletin.

content:
The prices to be charged for individual copies of and subscriptions to the code, the
   permanent supplements thereto and the bulletin, for reprints and bound volumes thereof
   and for pamphlet regulations, statements of policy, general rules and rules of court,
   which prices may be fixed without reference to the restrictions placed upon and fixed
   for the sale of other publications of the Commonwealth, and the number of copies which
   shall be distributed free for official use, shall be set by regulations promulgated
   by the joint committee.  Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, such regulations may provide for
   volume discounts available to established law book publishers who agree to incorporate
   fully the code, the permanent supplements thereto and the bulletin into their general
   scheme of promotion and distribution and may provide for the free reciprocal exchange
   of publications between this Commonwealth and other states and foreign jurisdictions
   and for the free distribution upon request of every publication printed under authority
   of this part to each:
